evidence: Paul's stated object is the head (11:7 τὴν κεφαλήν; 11:10 on the head)
Hair/shaving logic: uncovered = shorn (11:5-6; 14-15)
πρόσωπον absent; Paul names the face elsewhere when relevant (2 Cor 3:7,13,18; 1 Cor 13:12; 14:25)
LXX κατακαλύπτω: body-part object is the face 3/3 (Gen 38:15 mid.; Isa 6:2; Jer 28:51); never the head
Hermas Vis. 4.2.1: woman veiled 'to the forehead' with a mitra
Ps.-Dicaearchus (= Heraclides Criticus): Theban 'covering on the head' hides the whole face; the only Theban source
Roman matron's palla; Horace: only her face visible
Male capite velato (background to 11:4): head draped, face visible
Corinthian portraits mostly bare-headed; veiled ones show faces
Hellenistic tegidion: full-face veil with eye holes; Alexandria and Greek North Africa; 'not sure how far-flung'
verification: partly verified (author's own statement; book not obtained)
source: Llewellyn-Jones podcast 'Women Who Went Before' S2E3; Montier 2015 pp.14-15

evidence: Plutarch Greek Questions 49: Chalcedonian women veil one cheek before strange men/officials (living custom)
Josephus Ant. 7.254: absolute middle κατακαλυψαμένου for David's mourning; source (2 Sam 19:5) = covered his face
Susanna 32 (Th): married woman κατακεκαλυμμένη; unveiled so elders may feast on her beauty
Dio Chrysostom Or. 33.48-49: Tarsian women walk with faces covered; custom 'still in force' (survival of old strictness); NOT 'decaying'
source: Dio Or. 33.48-49; Payne 2015 n.45; Marlowe 2005 p.17

evidence: Num 5:18 LXX 'uncover the head'; m. Shabb. 6:6 Arabian women go out veiled (as distinctive)
Tertullian Virg. vel. 17: Christian women not covering face; Arab women cover face
Clement Paed. 3.11: entirely covered; not uncovering her face; pray veiled
Didascalia 1.8-9: head covered with robe; face veiled outdoors
Chrysostom Hom. 26 in 1 Cor: 'covered over ... wrapped up on every side'; silent on face
11:10 v.l. κάλυμμα (= 'head-covering, veil' per BDAG)
Jerome Ep. 130; Ambrose: praise face-veiling
